entry.title: Measles · US: CDC: 4,410 cases in 47 jurisdictions
entry.summary: The weekly update, with data as of 15 October, counts 4,410 confirmed cases, 42 new outbreaks this year and 451 hospitalisations. 96% of cases are linked to outbreaks. CDC counts 2 deaths; Pennsylvania reports 5 under its own definition. CDC also announced it will send an epidemiologist to support Pennsylvania's investigation.
entry.content:

CDC counts 2 deaths; Pennsylvania reports 5 under its own definition. CDC also announced it will send an epidemiologist to support Pennsylvania's investigation.

Sources: CDC: Measles cases and outbreaks, Detroit News (Reuters), ABC News, Contagion Live

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Media report Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
entry.summary: Reuters and Bloomberg report, citing health officials, two confirmed Ebola cases in North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic. Reuters says Congolese authorities had not yet officially announced the cases. It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.

It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.

Sources: Reuters via TimesLIVE, Bloomberg

entry.title: Dengue · Europe: Italy: 70 local dengue cases; France unchanged at 6
entry.summary: The ISS bulletin of 15 October counts 357 confirmed dengue cases from 1 January to 13 October; 70 were locally acquired, linked to 5 outbreaks plus 1 case not linked to the others, and there were no deaths. One of 30 chikungunya cases was locally acquired. Santé publique France's 14 October bulletin (data to 12 October) counts 4 local dengue episodes with 6 cases, with no new dengue episode, and 22 local chikungunya episodes with 162 cases.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a relative of the first patient, who was already in quarantine and under daily monitoring, tested positive after developing symptoms on 13 October. The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: WHO experts: Tumaini vaccine trial expected by end of October
entry.summary: WHO experts said the Tumaini trial in DR Congo is expected to begin by the end of October. It will first test Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire strain, to see whether it protects against Bundibugyo virus. Candidates from Oxford and Moderna, now in early-phase trials, may be added later. Whether Ervebo protects against this strain is not yet known.

Sources: AFP via Medical Xpress, CEPI

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: suspected cholera cases in Yemen roughly triple in three weeks
entry.summary: WHO says Yemen has recorded 8,034 suspected cholera cases and 27 deaths so far this year, and that weekly cases roughly tripled over three weeks. Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people (Abyan, Lahij, Al Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden) account for 92% of reported cases. WHO called for funding and access to safe water, vaccination and health services.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
entry.summary: Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.
entry.content:

Sources: IrCity, EANews, Kyiv Independent, Mediazona, The Moscow Times (Russian service)

entry.title: Plague · Russia: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:
WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
entry.summary: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".
entry.content:

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Kremlin calls most media reports false; second-case reports unconfirmed
entry.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the vast majority" of media reporting on the situation is false information and urged people to rely on Rospotrebnadzor's statements. Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets a second death; Russian officials have confirmed neither. WHO has asked Russia to clarify the reports.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: US asks Russia for more information; Putin call not yet arranged
entry.summary: A State Department spokesperson said the US has officially requested additional information from the Russian government. President Trump has said he plans to speak with President Putin about the case. The Kremlin said on 7 October that no call had been arranged yet but that it was open to one.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Bundibugyo vaccine trial begins in Uganda
entry.summary: The MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit vaccinated the first participants in Masaka City with a candidate vaccine developed by the University of Oxford. The early-phase study tests safety and immune response in healthy adults and follows a trial of the same candidate in the UK. It does not yet show whether the vaccine protects against the virus.
entry.content:

Sources: MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit, Xinhua, The Independent (Uganda)

entry.title: Plague · Russia: No plague found in contacts tested so far

entry.content:
Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.

entry.content:

Sources: UN News, NBC News, PBS NewsHour

CDC says cases with presumed domestic transmission have been reported in more than 10 jurisdictions and rates the risk to most people as low.
entry.content:

Sources: CDC: current situation, Medscape

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries
